To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the angular distributions of 2.5 keV electrons scattered elastically by helium were determined in the angular range of 2·10−3 to 4·10−3.
we have developed and tested an innovative method for the determination of the oscillator strengths of optical transitions in the helium atom by electron impact.
The angular distributions of 250 kev electrons scattered by helium were measured for the elastic scattering process and for excitation to the 21P, 31P, 41P and 52S states of helium.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elastic scattering and with the excitation of two optical transitions in helium.
a study of the scattering of 25 keV electrons by helium in the angular range between 2·3 and 4·10−3 radian.

the following problems:(1) The determination of the differential cross section for elastic scattering of electrons by helium atoms.(2) The determination of differential cross sections for excitation of optical states in helium by electron collision.(3) The determination of oscillator strength values for the 21 and 31 states in helium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the scattering theory of the Born approximation for the scattering of electrons on helium is in satisfactory agreement with experiment.
the experimental results are in satisfactory agreement with theory.
the experimental differential cross sections are in agreement with the scattering formulae of the present paper.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the scattering measurements have given a good check of the theoretical scattering formulae and that they have led to the determination of the oscillator strength of the 21S→21P and 21S→31P transition in helium.

the theoretical scattering formulae are in good agreement with experiment and the oscillator strengths of the 21 P and 31 P transitions in helium can be determined from the scattering cross sections with an accuracy of about 10%.

the experimental results are in agreement with theory and that the experimental values for the oscillator strengths of the 21 and 31 transitions are more accurate than any other values published so far.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of the Eckart wavefunction in the Born approximation leads to good agreement with the experimental data for the elastic scattering, and to a reasonable agreement for the inelastic scattering.
the elastic scattering cross section is not constant with angle.

the elastic scattering of electrons from helium can be described with a simple Born approximation, but that the inelastic scattering is much more complicated and cannot be described by a simple Born approximation.
